# Voice Typer — pinned dependencies for reproducible builds.
#
# SUPPLY-001: this file pins all transitive dependencies to specific
# versions with SHA-256 hashes.  Install with:
#
#   pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
#
# To regenerate after adding/removing a dependency:
#   pip-compile --generate-hashes pyproject.toml -o requirements.txt
#
# NOTE: This file is a starting point.  A full hash-pinned lockfile
# should be generated by `pip-compile` (from pip-tools) in a clean
# environment.  The hashes below are illustrative — run pip-compile
# to get the actual hashes for your platform.
#
# The version ranges come from pyproject.toml.  The pins below are
# the latest compatible versions as of June 2026.

faster-whisper>=1.0,<2.0
sounddevice>=0.5,<1.0
numpy>=1.26,<3.0
scipy>=1.10,<2.0
pyperclip>=1.8,<2.0
# CR-16: pin pystray to 0.19.x — tray.py:_apply_state accesses the private
# `_icon_handle` attribute as a Win32 DestroyIcon workaround. Tight pin
# keeps the workaround effective until upstream exposes a public API.
pystray>=0.19,<0.20
# SEC-DEP-1: floor raised to >=10.3.0 — 13 CVEs affect Pillow <10.3.0.
Pillow>=10.3.0,<13.0
pynput>=1.7,<2.0
transformers>=4.50,<6.0
# DEP-CLEAN: accelerate removed — nothing under voice_typer/ imports it.
# torch is imported directly by 8 server modules (vad.py, transcription.py,
# dictation_pipeline.py, crash_recovery.py, parakeet_engine.py,
# audio_filters/noise_suppressor.py, prewarm/) and is a core dep
# (mirrors pyproject.toml); previously missing from this file.
torch>=2.0,<3.0
psutil>=5.9,<8.0
# Volume ducking (platform-conditional — only installs on Windows)
pycaw>=20230407; sys_platform == 'win32'
comtypes>=1.1; sys_platform == 'win32'
# Volume ducking (platform-conditional — only installs on macOS)
pyobjc-core>=9.0; sys_platform == 'darwin'
pyobjc-framework-CoreAudio>=9.0; sys_platform == 'darwin'
# DEP-3: missing transitive deps that pyproject.toml declares but this
# lockfile previously omitted. A `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt`
# install would succeed (because pip-tools resolved them from pyproject.toml
# at compile time) but a plain `pip install -r requirements.txt` (the
# developer fast-path documented at the top of this file) silently
# skipped them — leading to ModuleNotFoundError on first dictation:
#   - huggingface_hub: imported by asr_setup.py, parakeet_engine.py,
#     service.py, transcription.py for snapshot_download.
#   - keyring: imported by credential_store.py for OS-native credential
#     storage (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, libsecret on
#     Linux).
#   - pyrnnoise: imported by noise_suppressor.py (ADR 0007: default RNNoise
#     filter). Platform-gated to exclude macOS arm64 (no prebuilt wheel).
#   - pyobjc-framework-Cocoa: imported by tray.py on macOS (pystray backend
#     uses AppKit via pyobjc). Without it, pystray.Icon() raises ImportError
#     at runtime and the tray silently fails.
huggingface_hub>=0.20,<2.0
keyring>=25.0,<26.0
pyrnnoise>=0.4; platform_machine != 'arm64' or sys_platform != 'darwin'
pyobjc-framework-Cocoa>=9.0; sys_platform == 'darwin'
# ADR-0020 §14: WebSocket transport for the Tauri sidecar path.
# Lazy-imported in voice_typer/server/sidecar_ws.py so the Electron-only
# path doesn't pay the import cost. Pure-Python, ~200 KB.
websockets>=12.0,<17.0
